Hand-in 1 · Brand · a name, a logo and one line
OSMEsaid oz-MAY · from the Greek osmē, scent

A tea bag that opens only at its perfect temperature.

NameOSME: osmē is Greek for scent. Every tea keeps its own.
LogoA tea bag whose string rises as an S of scent, amber where the water is hot, jade where it cools.
LineWhat it is, in one sentence. The tagline that carries it: "Every tea has its temperature."

Symbol: a tea bag whose string rises as an S of scent, amber where the water is hot, jade where it cools, and ends in a hanging tag. Bag, string and scent in one gesture; the S is OSME's own letter. Below 40 px use logo-symbol-small.svg: bag and one S, no tag.
Wordmark: Jost Medium, tracked +160, outlined so it looks the same everywhere. Always written OSME.
Mono black for light grounds, embossing and one-colour print; mono white (logo-*-mono.svg) for photos and colour fields. Clear space = the tag's width on every side.
BagThe product, plain and honest: paper white, tall, the classic shoulders.
String = scentosmē means scent. The string becomes the wisp that rises from the cup.
Arc in the lineThe temperature arc runs up the string: hot amber at the bag, cool jade at the tag.

Motif · Lu Yu's three bubble stages: fish eyes · string of pearls · rolling waves
Fish eyesFirst boil: small bubbles, a faint sound
String of pearlsSecond boil: bubbles rim the edge like pearls
Rolling wavesThird boil: the water surges
Type · Jost (embedded) for display and body
Patience, ritual, harmony.
Opens at the right heat · closes when it is done

Lu Yu read water by its bubbles. The tea bag traded that art for convenience a century ago. OSME brings it back: a bag that stays sealed until the water reaches its tea's ideal temperature, opens to brew, and closes again as the water cools.
